sources.entry: Build the game "Snake" in the terminal

summary.title: Programming Projects for Advanced Beginners #5: Snake
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a terminal version of the classic Snake game in six incremental milestones, covering board rendering, snake movement, death detection and apple eating.
takeaways: Split a game into Snake, Apple and Game classes, keeping each class's responsibilities small
Render a board by building a 2-D matrix of square states and then printing it with borders
Represent snake body as a list of coordinate tuples and directions as vectors such as UP = (0, 1)
Move the snake by adding a new head position and removing the tail, then detect death and eating apples
Build the prototype in small milestones, testing each before moving on
summary.summary: This project walks an advanced beginner through building a terminal Snake game in six milestones: setting up classes, rendering an empty bordered board, initializing and drawing a snake, accepting player input (W/A/S/D then Enter), detecting death on self-collision, and adding apples that grow the snake and increase the score. It recommends object-oriented design with Snake, Apple and Game classes and uses pseudo-code throughout, in any language. The article also argues for getting a working first version before worrying about design principles, and ends with a list of extension ideas such as multiple apples, 2-player mode and curses-based input.
